protoclim

Overview

protoclim is an R package for determining the climatic suitability of plant species and is intended to support risk assessors in performing a formal pest risk analysis. protoclim is heavily inspired and influenced by the Proto3 technique developed and used by the United States Department of Agriculture in their Guidelines for the USDA-APHIS PPQ Weed Risk Assessment Process.

protoclim is designed to be interoperable with any categorical climate variable but being inspired by the Proto3 model is intended to be used with:

  • Köppen-Geiger classes
  • Precipitation bands
  • Plant hardiness zones

Users are able to bring their own data but high-resolution global data has already been currated for each of the above climate variables by the associated repository protoclimData and is available for download from Zenodo. The climate variables are available across present-day and future time periods as well as various emission scenarios.

In addition to climate data, using protoclim requires species occurrence data from GBIF, the Global Biodiversity Information Facility. GBIF occurrence data can be downloaded from the GBIF website, the rgbif R package, or various other means.

protoclim comes with two datasets:

  1. bryonia_alba, GBIF occurrence data for Bryonia alba, the white bryony

  2. climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040, a lower-resolution version of the associated .tif file hosted on Zenodo.

Installation

The easiest way to get protoclim is to install it from CRAN:

install.packages("protoclim")

Development version

To get a bug fix or to use a feature from the development version, you can install the development version of protoclim from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("CFIA-PDAM/protoclim")
